### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. familial pityriasis rubra pilaris  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.731)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:16446)

**Proposed mechanism:** CARD14 (HGNC:16446) —INCREASES→ NF-kappaB signaling pathway (WP:WP414); NF-kappaB signaling pathway (WP:WP414) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal keratinocyte differentiation (HP:0030184); NF-kappaB signaling pathway (WP:WP414) —LEADS_TO→ Plaque psoriasis (HP:0011104); NF-kappaB signaling pathway (WP:WP414) —LEADS_TO→ Erythroderma (HP:0010563). Gain-of-function mutations in CARD14 lead to constitutive activation of the NF-kappaB signaling pathway, which in turn drives abnormal keratinocyte differentiation, manifesting as the shared phenotype of plaque psoriasis and related conditions like erythroderma.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that the mutations in CARD14 associated with MONDO:0011269 are loss-of-function, while those in familial pityriasis rubra pilaris are gain-of-function, or vice-versa. _(variant: Identification of common variants (AF > 1%) in the canonical CARD14 transcript in gnomAD that are associated with either disease.)_

**Why it matters:** Targeting the CARD14-NF-kappaB signaling axis could offer a unified therapeutic strategy for both MONDO:0011269 and familial pityriasis rubra pilaris, potentially by inhibiting upstream activators or downstream effectors of this pathway.
